summary.value: The Slovenian Silver Hen is a white-feathered laying chicken bred by poultry scientists at the University of Ljubljana in Slovenia, where the line was settled and tested around 1968. Breeders favored a sex-linked gene for silver-white plumage, which makes the hens useful as a parent line. Crossed with Slovenian Brown roosters, they produce the commercial Prelux Brown layer. The hens are plain white with yellow legs, yellow-orange eyes, a medium single comb and small pale red earlobes. Roosters weigh about 6 to 7 pounds and hens about 4.9 to 5.3 pounds. A hen starts laying at around five months and gives some 260 to 270 brown eggs a year, each weighing about 64 grams, larger than the eggs of the other Slovenian breeds. Most of the flock, a little over 900 birds in 2020, is kept at the university's poultry center.
